label: early-sequence token after an l/c/q prefix ending in c (e.g. l c c [u])
explanation: Sparse feature (0.014% of steps) that fires almost only in the original phase at t=2-4 (about 97% of mass), plus a weak echo on <DEL> right after short sequences like l c c q. It behaves like an additive conjunction of the recent prefix: the sequence starts with l (first_tok l has 17x lift, c and 3 weaker), the previous input is c (25x lift; q 5x, l 2x), the token two back is c, l or q, and the current token comes from a preferred set (u, t, h, q, y, b, j, l, 1, 0, z). The strongest activations are on exact patterns like l c c [u], l l c [u], l q c [t], at 0.9-1.0 of max. Fewer matching ingredients means weaker activations (for example l q [u] or x c q [j] at about 0.43). The prototype l, {l,c,q}, c, X-in-set is about 97% precise but covers only 27% of mass. The best simple predicate gets F1 0.53. It never fires in the copy phase (t > L) or at t=0-1, and almost never at t >= 5. Because the response is graded and additive, no single boolean clause captures it fully.
